text: Direct regulation of hedge fund leverage increases moral hazard costs, because lenders and counterparties relax their own vigilance once they rely on government rules to constrain fund risk taking.
citation: Kaal and Oesterle, The History of Hedge Fund Regulation in the United States (2016). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2714974

isBasedOn.name: The History of Hedge Fund Regulation in the United States

abstract: Direct regulation could also increase moral hazard costs as lenders and counterparties may relax their vigilance in reliance on the government rules.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: applies where government rules substitute for private monitoring
